title: feature suggestion: playback streams shortcuts
line: Every application that plays sound now gets shortcuts in System Settings to raise, lower and mute its own volume.
explanation: The Audio Volume shortcuts could only change the default output device or microphone, so controlling a single application's volume from a key (e.g. a macro pad) needed a pactl/pw-cli script, with no on-screen feedback. Now plasma-pa's kded registers three shortcuts in the Audio Volume group for each application that is playing sound: Increase Volume of <app>, Decrease Volume of <app> and Mute <app>. They change all of that application's streams by the usual volume step and show the OSD with the application's name and icon ("Strawberry 55%", "Strawberry Muted"). Entries without a shortcut disappear when the application stops playing; entries with a shortcut stay and are registered again at login, so the shortcut keeps working the next time the application plays.

commits.message:
kded: add volume and mute shortcuts for each playing application

Volume shortcuts could only change the output device, so changing one
application's volume needed a script. Every application playing sound now
gets shortcuts to raise, lower and mute it, which stay while one is set.

BUG: 508929

media.caption: Strawberry is playing, but Shortcuts → Audio Volume only has system-wide volume actions
Audio Volume now lists Increase/Decrease Volume of Strawberry and Mute Strawberry; Meta+Alt+PgUp assigned
Pressing the shortcut raises only Strawberry (50% → 55%) and shows its name in the OSD; system volume stays at 30%
Mute Strawberry mutes just that application, with a "Strawberry Muted" OSD
